result.summary: This PR threads BCLog::Logger/util::log::Logger instances through kernel-adjacent classes (BlockManager, CDBWrapper, CCoinsViewDB, Chainstate, ChainstateManager, CoinsViews, CTxMemPool) so libbitcoinkernel applications can control where kernel log output goes instead of it always flowing to one global logger. It also drops the always-allocated global Logger instance, adds a LOG_REQUIRE_CONTEXT compile-time option, and migrates many legacy LogPrint/LogPrintf calls in validation.cpp and elsewhere to the newer log macros. It is presented as a narrower alternative to the closed #30338 RFC and sits on top of three other open logging PRs (#34778, #29256, #33847).
result.problem: Kernel embedders currently cannot separate or scope log output per ChainstateManager/mempool instance; everything goes through one implicit global logger, which limits multi-instance or library use cases and forces a fixed 1MB pre-buffering scheme. This mainly affects prospective libbitcoinkernel consumers, not typical bitcoind users.

open_concerns: stickies-v (member): Approach NACK — the contextualized-logging interface is easy to misuse (forgetting to pass a context silently falls back to the global logger) and adds nontrivial review/merge-conflict cost for a benefit nobody has concretely demonstrated needing yet.
resolved_concerns: Author proposed a LOG_REQUIRE_CONTEXT enforcement mechanism to prevent silent fallback to the global logger; stickies-v accepted it as 'elegant' and did not continue pressing the objection, instead opening a smaller alternative PR (#34775) addressing the same underlying interface-weirdness concern more pragmatically.

result.card: This PR threads Logger instances through libbitcoinkernel classes (BlockManager, CDBWrapper, CCoinsViewDB, ChainstateManager, CTxMemPool) so kernel-embedding applications can direct log output away from a single global logger, and it removes the previously always-leaked global Logger allocation. It solves a real but so-far undemonstrated need for multi-instance/library logging control, mainly benefiting prospective libbitcoinkernel consumers rather than bitcoind users. A reviewer (stickies-v) gave Concept ACK but Approach NACK, arguing the added interface complexity and 25+-PR conflict surface outweigh the benefit absent a concrete use case, then opened a simpler competing PR (#34775) rather than continuing to block; the author's counter-proposal (a compile-time context-enforcement mechanism) was well received but didn't fully resolve the skepticism. The PR is draft, labeled Needs rebase, has required 50 force-pushes over more than two years, and depends on three other open logging PRs (#34778, #29256, #33847), making it Stale for review purposes despite the author remaining active. Priority is moderate (P3) in kernel and utils where the architectural change is real, and low (P4) in validation, indexes, and tools where the diff is mechanical plumbing that follows from the interface change elsewhere.
